First, we express

$$
f(x)=(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))^{7}.
$$

Now, we see that $f(x)$ can be expressed as the composite function

$$
f={u}^{7},\,u=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=7{u}^{6},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =7{u}^{6}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\  & =7{sin}^{6}⁡(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$
